correctness.rationale: The proof checks exact query semantics and all quantifiers. For small irrational slopes, the last-positive arc cannot support all four first-pair patterns due to end-anchored intervals, and a dense return gives a shattered pair; for larger slopes, at most six boundaries on a final-positive arc forbid shattered quadruples, while a disjoint-complement construction yields a shattered triple. Pair/triple supports are characterized by open circle cells. The density limit follows from weighted irrational equidistribution. A standard-library checker independently verified 7,808 finite exact-arithmetic trace comparisons; no universal conclusion relies on finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: Primary literature gives the constant mask dimension two (Muller) and the general one-unit variable-length gap (Johnson), hence a pre-existing upper bound three. The claimed exact slope-dependent 2/3 transition and all shattered pair/triple supports are not consequences of those bounds or of the inspected nearby published records. Direct published-finding corpus, web and ledger claim searches produced no stronger implication. Full Muller preprint unavailable, so historical priority is qualified.
residual_risks: The full 2005 Muller preprint could not be inspected; only its accessible abstract, which addresses arbitrary fixed windows, was reviewed. An appendix might contain stronger, directly covering claims.
Unindexed or differently worded mathematical or computer-science work could already establish the same exact slope dichotomy. Search absence is not uniqueness proof.
No independent review has been performed; the phase-arc argument is presented for same-model review only.
